approach: Scope is issue #339's M3 + M4 only. Its M1/M2 (upstream library barrel, multi-entry exports, dts, envPrefix on the probe) already shipped in cyber-mux 0.3.0, so nothing upstream blocks this CR.

M3: add cyber-mux as a pinned dependency, retarget every import site onto it, and delete the forked src/console except doorbell.ts, which carries mail and turn-taking semantics rather than multiplexer semantics.

M4: retire the env-namespace drift by migrating the fast-path vars to the cyber-mux namespace. Owner-ratified live, chosen over the envPrefix compatibility route and over blocking on a further upstream change.

The namespace migration rewrites frozen scenarios on the mux node, so it takes a re-open and a Clearance grant. The owner selected the option whose statement named both, which is the pre-authorization. Classify the edit class structurally with gherkin-cli diff rather than from a line diff.

Panes already live in the fleet carry the old fast-path vars, so a transitional normalization maps the old pair onto the new one when only the old is present. Separately deletable once the window closes.
Adopt the package's own exec seam outright rather than asserting structural compatibility between two copies, per the issue's stated preference for one seam.

Widening the pane-multiplexer union to the two additional backends the package supports is deliberately out of scope: the union is persisted on the unit record, so widening is its own change request. Filed as a follow-up.

Controls that must survive: a real open, send, read and close round-trip against a live multiplexer, since the fleet runs units against this seam; and every deleted test accounted for rather than dropped.

why: Namespace migration rewrites frozen scenarios on the mux node; the owner granted Clearance live before drafting by selecting the option whose statement named both the rewrite and the floor. Structural diff 7 added / 3 modified / 3 removed, every removed one a retitle whose replacement is among the added — no behavior dropped, re-verified independently by the cold judge in two separate rounds. Four cold spec-judge rounds: a governance pre-flight miss, then two real defects (a precedence-tier contradiction and a duplicated sibling fact), then a section-order defect the prior remediation itself introduced, then aligned on all three lenses with 26 of 26 scenarios clean.

cause: producer declared one of seven required governance bars, so the first judge round short-circuited at pre-flight without grading any lens

adding a precedence tier to a first-match-wins chain without re-auditing the lower-tier siblings' preconditions to exclude it, producing a constructible state on which three scenarios demanded different answers
restating a sibling node's owned constraint as free-standing fact in two places instead of referencing the node that owns it
appending the newly required sections after a pre-existing one rather than relocating it, which wedged an unsanctioned section into the mandated order

why: Three cold impl-judge rounds, each finding a real verification gap the previous round missed. All 26 frozen scenarios are now individually mutation-proven; the consumed dependency was restored byte-for-byte after every mutation and checksum-verified against the published tarball. Also verified against a live multiplexer: a real spawn opened a real pane and worktree, mail delivered, and the reaper discriminated — culling nothing while the pane lived and the record once it died.

cause: two scenarios had no verification because the end-to-end harness strips the very environment their precondition needs, so both assertions ran with nothing detected and checked only that a label was present

deleting a forked layer took its tests with it on the reasoning that the upstream package covers them; upstream coverage protects the package's behavior, not this project's frozen contract, leaving eight scenarios with no regression protection
a commit message claimed a rename would make the scenario bridge bind these scenarios, but only seven of twenty-six bound because one test file was never wrapped

note: The herdr backend's no-focus flag on tab and workspace creation is asserted by no test, unlike the tmux equivalent. Same blind-spot species this mission closed for the focus probes, left open here.
No test passes an explicit tab placement under tmux; coverage leans on that backend treating tab and workspace as one branch, which is true today but unasserted.

The mode verb's catch-all reports no-multiplexer for any thrown error, including the detected-but-unsupported refusal, so it cannot name the backend the spawn verb names. No frozen scenario covers the combination.

The multiplexer package's pane enumeration no longer filters panes with no agent, which the fork did. The registry's own adoption path re-implements the filter so nothing is broken today, but the reconcile cull's live set now includes panes it previously excluded. Belongs to the registry node.

The transitional legacy-variable read treats a pair as present or absent as a whole, so a half-set current pair suppresses the legacy pair rather than filling the missing half. No frozen scenario exercises a half-set pair; the contract is silent on it.

The storable-multiplexer set stays at two while the package drives four. Widening it is a change to the registry node because the value is persisted on the unit record, and was deliberately out of scope here. This is the third open question on the originating issue.

Upstream: the package's self-identity helper hardcodes its own variable namespace and takes no prefix option, unlike its probe. A host adopting the package under its own namespace therefore needs a normalization seam it would not otherwise need. Belongs to the package's repository, not this one.

Most blocks in the spawn test file straddle two spec nodes, so they stay unbound to the scenario bridge and every judge round re-derives them by hand. Splitting the file by node would let the bridge carry them.
